en.title: Last Stone Weight
en.description:
Each turn, take the two heaviest stones and smash them together. If their weights are equal, both are destroyed; otherwise the lighter one is destroyed and the heavier one is left with the difference of the two weights. Repeat until at most one stone remains, then output the weight of the last stone; output 0 if there are no stones.

The problem rules, examples, and n/weight constraints are complete.

This site adds the standard input/output protocol; it does not imply that the original site's function-style problem had this protocol.
en.input: The first line contains n (1 ≤ n ≤ 100000), and the second line contains n positive integers weights[i] (1 ≤ weights[i] ≤ 10^9).
en.output: Output the weight of the last remaining stone; output 0 if all stones are destroyed.
en.explanation: See the accompanying notes for the problem rules, the approach, and the proof.
hints: Use a max-heap to repeatedly take out the two heaviest stones; if they are not equal, push the difference back into the heap.
